title: Optional, default, and rest parameters
hook: Optional parameters, default values, and rest parameters are real JavaScript features — TypeScript adds rules about which parameters can be omitted and how they appear in the emitted code.

sections.heading: What are optional and rest parameters?

blocks.text: **Optional parameters** use `?`: `function f(x?: number)` — callers may omit the argument; inside the function it is `number | undefined`. **Default parameters** assign when `undefined` is passed: `function f(x = 10)`. **Rest parameters** collect trailing args: `function f(...ids: string[])`. Unlike C# `params`, rest must be last. TypeScript checks arity at compile time; JavaScript applies defaults and packs rest at **runtime** — the behavior you debug in production.

entries.plainDefinition: Parameter callers may omit — typed as T | undefined inside.
Used when argument is undefined (not other falsy unless explicit).
Collects remaining arguments into an array.
Number of required parameters — TS enforces at call sites.
entries.example: f(a, b?) requires at least one arg

blocks.text: API design: optional config objects vs many positional params. Default parameters enable **optional trailing args without overloads**. Rest replaces `arguments` object (typed). C# optional params use `[Optional]` or default values at call site — similar ergonomics, different overload resolution. Misordering optional before required is a compile error in TS.

blocks.body: function f(x?: number, y: string) — compile error. Reorder or use options object.

blocks.text: Default parameter expressions evaluate left-to-right at call time — later defaults can reference earlier params. Destructuring in params: function f({ a, b = 1 }: Opt). Tuple rest for fixed-prefix variadic: (head: string, ...tail: number[]). For overload-like arity, use overload signatures or union rest tuples.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected
blocks.body: Thinking default handles null. Putting required after optional. Using arguments instead of typed rest.

interviewTakeaways: Optional ? and default = both allow omission; default applies on undefined only.
Rest ...args: T[] must be last — replaces arguments.
Options object scales better than many optional positionals.
60s: Required first, then optional/default, rest last. Default not null. TS checks arity. C# params similar. Runtime is plain JS.
commonPitfalls: Weak: null triggers default parameter — only undefined does.
Weak: optional param before required — compile error.
Strong: Options object for 3+ opts. Rest for variadic. Destructure with defaults in signature.

jsTsCorrelations.note: ES2015 defaults and rest are runtime features — TypeScript adds arity and type checking.
When arity changes return type, overloads complement optional params.
